bug_semantics: SoupServer handle_partial_get() honors a request Range by slicing the accumulated response body with g_bytes_new_from_bytes(full_response, ranges[i].start, ranges[i].end - ranges[i].start + 1). soup_message_headers_get_ranges_internal() treated a range as unsatisfiable only when cur.start >= total_length; a valid start with cur.end past the body was still returned as 206 Partial Content. GLib g_bytes_new_from_bytes() bounds checks are compiled out under G_DISABLE_CHECKS, so the oversized slice can read and return heap past the intended body (CWE-125). The same unbounded slice existed earlier via soup_buffer_new_subbuffer(), which performed no length check at all.
flaw_origin: The first public write of both halves of the mechanism is 264eb7480e3a1c5762e4eb51f8273e6e438ff87b (Dan Winship, 2008-10-01, svn r1176): soup_message_headers_get_ranges() parsed Range ends with g_ascii_strtoull and never clamped/rejected cur.end against total_length, and handle_partial_get() immediately used those values in soup_buffer_new_subbuffer(). Parent 91d657fb12308d51608dd3f6b6c4b3fa6b117bee has neither function. 8524d461 later added a start-only satisfiability check; 4b43e158 is a SoupBuffer-to-GBytes refactor of the same slice and is not the BIC.
